name: Saint Maarten
rule: Sint Maarten LVV plant controls still do not classify manufactured sencha. Separately, current Landsbesluit publieke gezondheid (AB 2017 no.33), article 4(2), confines food import notification to commercial use. Article 4(3) confines origin health certificates to commercial imports of dairy, fish, poultry/meat and baby food; plain tea is not listed. Its official explanatory note distinguishes personal from commercial use by presentation, packaging and quantity, without a passenger-only limitation. This narrows the unresolved issue to the separate plant-health classification rather than imposing commercial food paperwork on a 100g private parcel.
personalMailApplicability: The public-health notification/certificate duties are limited by intended commercial use, not by whether a seller was paid or by a traveler-only allowance. Treating a single 100g parcel intended for the recipient’s own consumption as personal follows the enacted scope and explanatory note. Independent LVV plant-product scope remains unverified.
authority: Sint Maarten LVV; Ministry of Public Health, Social Development and Labor; official local legislation register
remainingQuestion: Current legal basis and operative scope for LVV plant-produce controls, including any law/conditions adopted after the official2022policy explicitly said plant-protection legislation was being developed. The current LVV administrative page is broader than that historical legal account but has no manufactured-food definition. Public-health private-use scope is resolved.
researchAttempts: Reviewed Sint Maarten LVV plant-import guidance and application material. No manufactured-tea or personal-mail entry identified.

2026-09-30: Retrieved the government’s complete AB 2017 no.33 Public Health Decree PDF and checked its current official register, which marks it effective 27 July 2018 to present. Read article 4(1)–(3), the import-notice form, and official explanatory note on PDF pages 39–41. Notification is limited to commercial consumption goods; health certification is additionally limited to listed animal foods/baby food. The note expressly distinguishes personal use based on presentation/quantity and repeats the commercial limit. A 2020 Inspectorate release reproduced by news outlets describes personal food up to 10 kg, but that secondary numerical threshold was not promoted into a primary-source quantity limit. Kept overall unresolved solely because independent LVV manufactured-tea classification remains missing.

2026-09-30 fresh official online recovery: Recovered the current official LVV page HTML and checked its links/media. The Import Export Conditions item is an image without linked commodity conditions; the available forms concern small animals. This yields no processed-tea import rule. The independently verified Public Health Decree personal-food scope remains intact; unresolved issue is the separate LVV plant-product classification. Saved sx-lvv.html.

30 September renewed official-source/general-definition review: Targeted official government/legal searches for plant imports, processed products and phytosanitary tea returned no new operative plant-product definition. The existing government plant-produce form remains an application instrument, not an exhaustive definition/list; examples of seeds, cuttings, fruits and plants neither affirmatively include nor exclude manufactured sencha. The independently recovered 2017 Public Health Decree commercial-use limitation remains favorable for this private order and is not displaced by older commercial exporter summaries. No fresh exemption or permit duty is inferred.

30 September operative-source recovery: Retrieved complete approved2022AgriculturePolicy from current www government host after the legacy www1 link served a construction page. Section5.2(p16/17) says agriculture regulations/plant-protection laws were still being developed and identifies Commodities Act(former1997NAFoodLaw334) as governing food/agricultural products. This is positive historical evidence about legislative status, not just an empty search. Current LVV page nevertheless describes import monitoring for plants/plant produce without publishing a manufacturing definition; targeted2025/26 official-source checks yielded no operative successor. No2026 exemption is inferred from a2022policy. Existing current2017public-health private-use conclusion preserved.
